# Static site regenerated by a scheduled job; no server, no database

A scheduled job runs once or twice a day, reads every Feed, updates a committed data file of Items, and rebuilds a static site from it. Nothing runs between builds.

## Why

The project is a personal one with near-zero budget, meant to be handed off someday. A static site on free hosting plus a scheduled job has no monthly bill and nothing to babysit. Nothing on the source list changes faster than daily: agendas are posted 72 hours ahead by law, and press releases and events are not minute-critical.

## Considered options

- Always-on server with a database and live polling. Rejected: cost, upkeep, and no source that needs it.
- Static site (chosen).

## Consequences

Freshness is bounded by the job schedule. Features that need per-user state (accounts, keyword alerts, email digests) are deferred; RSS per Topic is the subscription mechanism at launch. The committed data file is the system of record, so its history lives in git.
